item.title: Why Lakers’ Luka Doncic gave Cameron Carr the game ball after win over Hawks
item.description: Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Why Lakers’ Luka Doncic gave Cameron Carr the game ball after win over Hawks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Monday, the Los Angeles Lakers won their 10th game of the season in 12 tries after grabbing a 124-114 victory over the Atlanta Hawks on the second night of a back-to-back. Of course, it was Luka Doncic who led the way once again. Fresh off a rest day on Sunday, Doncic lit up the Hawks to the tune of 32 points, 10 rebounds, and eight assists — continuing his torrid start to the 2026-27 campaign. But it wasn’t Doncic who brought home the game ball. Not even Sandro Mamukelashvili, who put up 23 points and eight boards off the bench, took the ball home with him, nor did Walker Kessler or Collin Sexton. It was Lakers guard Cameron Carr who did so, with Doncic actually giving him the game ball to celebrate a major accomplishment — scoring his first career points in the NBA. “You always want to remember your first bucket, you know. And you want to get that ball so it was, you know, kind of important for me to grab it. He was good, he was very good. It’s not easy to just get in the game and play the game so he was very good. He’s just got to keep building on it,” Doncic said after the game, via Spectrum SportsNet on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Luka gave Cam Carr the game ball after scoring his first NBA points in tonight's win over Atlanta! pic.twitter.com/tAT0n4ie2h — Spectrum SportsNet (@SpectrumSN) November 10, 2026 Prior to tonight’s ballgame, Carr has played in a grand total of three minutes in the NBA, failing to score a single point and missing his only field-goal attempt. The Lakers have been bringing the rookie along slowly after he suffered an injury in preseason, and with the absence of Austin Reaves and Quentin Grimes against the Hawks, Carr earned the opportunity to suit up for more than just one garbage-time minute. The Lakers are high on Carr’s potential, but it looks like he will be spending his rookie season as more of a spectator, especially amid the team’s hot start. But if, knock on wood, LA faces some injury problems, Carr should remain ready in case head coach JJ Redick calls upon his number. item.title: Warriors fans react to “coach Jimmy Butler” as he had just one instruction in win against Pelicans
item.description: Photo by KARIM JAAFAR/AFP via Getty Images The Golden State Warriors had a dominant win against the New Orleans Pelicans, and Jimmy Butler adorned the role of the coach during the game. The vibes around the Golden State Warriors are immaculate right now, with the veteran roster finding a healthy balance with exciting youngsters. Yaxel Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski lent Steph Curry a hand this time as the Warriors dominated the Pelicans in a 51-point win. However, the moment of the game was when Jimmy Butler took over as coach, and he had just one instruction for his players. Warriors fans on “coach Jimmy Butler” The likes of Steph Curry and Draymond Green are almost having another prime right now as the rookies have brought them right back to contention. The same is true for Jimmy Butler, who wouldn’t have expected to return to a winning team this season, let alone a contender. That mood was clear to see during the Warriors’ win against the Pelicans, as Steve Kerr “consulted” with Jimmy Butler during a timeout, who was wearing full coaching attire. He was having fun with it, soon “drawing up a play” that simply read “Pass to Steph”, prompting Warriors fans to react hilariously. “Vibes are immaculate. This is the year they let Iggy [Andre Iguodala] coach too,” said one, as a second said, “Holding that board like he’s the real one,” with three laughing emojis. A third said, “Looks like it is going to be early time off for Steph today, as it should,” as another said, “Top 1 team chemistry”. Warriors fans also trolled Steve Kerr after Butler “leaked” Kerr’s playbook of “Pass to Steph”. “Steve Kerr’s $35m playbook just got leaked on national television and Jimmy just boiled down 15 years of NBA wisdom,” said one fan, as another said, “Coach Jimmy got one play in the book and it’s the right one.” A third joked, “That’s all Kerr has had to draw for the last ten years and it has worked out perfectly,” as another wrote, “’22 team chemistry vibes,” thinking back to the surprise winners in 2022. No return date for Butler is set yet, but he’s contributing to the team atmosphere in different ways to keep a good thing going. item.title: ‘Didn’t know much about him’: DeMarcus Cousins says his favourite Lakers player is not Luka Doncic
item.description: Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images Luka Doncic is the biggest star in the Los Angeles Lakers’ locker room. The Slovenian is one of the best in the business, and if he continues at the same rate, he will likely win the MVP award this season. That is why Doncic is almost everybody’s favourite Lakers player, but DeMarcus Cousins’ pick is actually someone else. DeMarcus Cousins says Walker Kessler is his favourite Lakers player Walker Kessler joined the Los Angeles Lakers in July via a sign-and-trade deal on a four-year, $130 million contract. The 25-year-old had made a terrific name for himself while playing for the Utah Jazz, and his game has gone up a level since moving to LA. Kessler usually starts at centre alongside Doncic, and even though it’s the latter who makes all the headlines, the former has mostly been incredible as well. Cousins has watched a lot of the Lakers this season, and he has named Kessler as his favourite player ahead of the likes of Doncic and Austin Reaves. He said on the Run The Ball show: “My favourite player in this team is Walker Kessler. “I didn’t know much about him in Utah, but the way he controls the paint and the way he protects the rim… He had a few incredible blocks against Ausar Thompson, who is a freak athlete.” Cousins then had his say on the Lakers, a team he had made fun of before the start of the season. He has now held his hands up and admitted that they deserve respect. He said: “This is a pretty well-rounded team. Early on, there were a lot of jokes. I was one of the main people joking. It didn’t quite look great on paper. But seeing how this team is starting to shape up, you’ve got to put some respect on this Lakers group and the guys on this team. “Reaves is playing at an All-Star level right now. He put on an incredible performance. I love everything I’m seeing from this Lakers team right now.” The Lakers really are looking good, and everyone on the team, like Kessler, is producing the goods on a consistent basis. That, combined with Doncic playing out of his skin and looking like the next MVP, gives the Los Angeles side a great chance of going all the way this season. item.title: Cooper Flagg Matches NBA History As Mavericks Beat Pacers
item.description: Cooper Flagg Mavericks Getty Dallas Mavericks superstar Cooper Flagg matched NBA history as the Mavericks beat the Indiana Pacers 125-122 on Monday night. The Mavericks improved to 7-4 on the season with the nail-biter victory over Indiana, which dropped to 3-8, on the back of another amazing performance by Flagg, who, at just 19 years of age, continues to show he is one of the NBA’s best players. Cooper Flagg Has Historic Game for Mavericks With 43 points, 10 rebounds, and 6 assists, Flagg joined NBA legend Kevin Durant as the only two rookies in NBA history to have a 40/10/5 game, per theScore. Cooper Flagg is just the second teenager (Kevin Durant) in NBA history with 40/10/5 in a game. 🤯 pic.twitter.com/X89SflYcdt — theScore (@theScore) November 10, 2026 It was an absolutely incredible performance by Flagg, who has morphed into one of the NBA’s top players in his second NBA season. Cooper Flagg Is Having an Amazing Year for Dallas In February 2025, the Mavericks made one of the worst trades in the history of professional sports when they sent Luka Doncic to the Los Angeles Lakers for Anthony Davis, Max Christie, and a first-round pick. The only good thing about that trade was that the Mavericks tanked in the standings, ended up winning the NBA Draft Lottery, and took Flagg with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft. In Flagg’s rookie season last year, he averaged 21 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 5.4 assists in 70 games and won the NBA Rookie of the Year Award. This year, Flagg has gotten even better, as he’s averaging 25.9 points, 6.9 rebounds, and 6.9 assists per game through the early goings-on of the season. Not only that, but the Mavericks are winning games and look like they could be a dark-horse contender for a playoff spot. If the Mavericks do end up making the playoffs, Flagg may end up getting down-ballot MVP consideration, as he’s been that good for Dallas, which has been a pleasant surprise this year. There is obviously a ton of time left in the season, and the Mavericks need Flagg to stay healthy if they are going to go anywhere this year. But provided he does, they may sneak into the playoffs and could even make some noise if Flagg takes an even bigger leap in his game in the postseason. item.description: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Greg Rousseau gives Vikings defense props for challenging Josh Allen appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Minnesota Vikings took on Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. The Vikings wanted to regroup after a loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 8. Unfortunately for them, the Bills were up to the task . Buffalo defeated Minnesota on the road on Monday Night Football. Allen had a good game, passing for 234 yards, but had to work for everything he got. Bills defender Greg Rousseau gave the Vikings defense their flowers after the game . “They’re a really good defense. Against the run, the pass, they’re unpredictable. The blitzing on second and long, and third down. They come at you with a lot of looks so it’s a challenge for our offense. But our offense really took that challenge, and faced it head on. They didn’t back down,” Rousseau said, via ESPN’s Scott Van Pelt. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Vikings defense certainly got after Allen in this one. He threw an interception in this game and was sacked four times. But when it mattered most, Buffalo was able to punch through Minnesota’s tough defense to claim victory. It certainly helped that the Bills defense came to play in this one. The Vikings offense managed less than 200 yards of total offense. The Bills forced two fumbles, and held Vikings signal-caller Carson Wentz to less than 100 yards passing. It was a complete performance for the Bills. As for Minnesota, they have lost consecutive games after beginning the season 6-0. The Vikings will look to get back on track in Week 10 when they travel to Lambeau Field to take on the Green Bay Packers. item.description: Phillies predicted to sign $15M three-time All-Star slugger over Japanese phenom Teruaki Sato originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Phillies know their window to win another World Series is beginning to narrow. With several members of their core group getting older, the pressure is mounting for the organization to make the most of its championship opportunity. Philadelphia has several areas to address this offseason following another disappointing postseason. One of the biggest priorities will be improving the outfield, which remains an area of concern heading into next season. “Of the areas that the team needs to address, not much has changed over the last couple of years. This is still a group that needs more offensively from their outfield and also better pitching from the bullpen. In terms of free agency, these should certainly be the areas that they are focused on, but it might not be the only one," SI's Nick Ziegler wrote. The Phillies have been mentioned as a potential landing spot for Japanese star Teruaki Sato, who currently plays third base but could eventually transition to the outfield. “Some teams believe he can stay at third base; others see him as best suited for first base or left field. Either way, the bat profiles for the middle of the order. I think he stays at third base initially and would be a perfect fit for teams like the Phillies, Red Sox, Angels and Yankees, which leads me to believe this will end up being a big-market bidding war," MLB insider Jim Bowden wrote. While signing Sato would certainly generate excitement among Philadelphia fans, CBS Sports' Dayn Perry believes the organization could pursue Seattle Mariners outfielder Randy Arozarena instead. “Arozarena is coming off an excellent season with Seattle, and the Phillies , still trying to make the most of their closing window, badly need an upgrade at the outfield corners. Philly hasn't been shy about investing in the on-field product, which means adding the likes of Arozarena would be fully in character,” Perry wrote. Adding a former ALCS MVP would bring valuable postseason experience to Philadelphia's outfield. More importantly, Arozarena could provide a significant boost to a Phillies lineup that struggled with consistency at times last season. Arozarena recently completed his $15 million contract with the Seattle Mariners, potentially making him an intriguing option for Philadelphia. With its championship window narrowing, the Phillies could be aggressive in pursuing an established bat who can help them make another deep postseason run. item.title: Arsenal have already blown their WSL title chances - but Gunners still have the talent to win another Women's Champions League
item.description: Arsenal UWCL hopes GFX - Getty/GOAL Renee Slegers' side have underwhelmed domestically this season, but as huge games with Barcelona and Lyon approach, opportunity knocks for them to remind everyone they could still be capable of something special in Europe With nine games gone in the Women's Super League season, Arsenal sit sixth in the standings, having gathered just 13 points to sit a massive 12 off the pace of leaders Manchester City. Even at this early stage, their hopes of lifting a first WSL title since 2019 look doomed. Yet, as strange as it may seem given their struggles, that does not mean they should be overlooked in the Champions League. It's not been smooth-sailing in the early knockings of their European adventure by any means. A narrow 1-0 win over HB Koge in their first outing was a real struggle, with the Danes unlucky not to get anything from a game won by Mariona Caldentey's stoppage-time penalty . Then came an eventful 2-2 draw away at Paris FC, where an inexplicable handball by Leah Williamson allowed the hosts to complete their comeback from 2-0 down . At the time, there was a feeling that could be the final game for head coach Renee Slegers. But the Dutchwoman remains at the helm as the Gunners prepare for a huge couple of weeks in this competition having overseen a much more convincing 3-0 win over Benfica in the team's last European outing. Now, two huge tests beckon: away at Barcelona, the reigning champions , on Thursday before the hosting of eight-time winners Lyon a week later. It's a great chance for Arsenal, winners of this competition just 18 months ago , to remind everyone what they are capable of. Slow starters Arsenal have a history of starting seasons slowly, with them still able to come on strong in the latter stages of the previous two campaigns Many will argue that Arsenal don't deserve to be spoken about as Champions League contenders after their start to the season. The Gunners have regularly looked out of ideas, defensively weak and unable to maximise the talent in this squad, which was massively increased by what looked, on paper, like an outstanding transfer window . But it is worth noting that Arsenal have a history of starting seasons slowly. It was that which ultimately cost the Gunners a shot at the WSL title last term, with them only finishing four points behind eventual winners City in the end. Regrets were traced back to September and October, where draws against Manchester United and Aston Villa proved costly before a defeat to City. It meant their subsequent 17-game unbeaten streak in the league was somewhat in vain. A year previous, a run of one win from the opening four league games would spell the end of Jonas Eidevall's time in charge. It was another campaign in which Arsenal were the closest rivals to the eventual WSL champion, but they were nowhere near an invincible Chelsea in the end. item.title: What made Youri Tielemans’ first Man United strike unique in Premier League era
item.description: What made Youri Tielemans’ first Man United strike unique in Premier League era Manchester United’s Youri Tielemans opened his account for the Red Devils at the weekend. Goalscoring The Belgian is not renowned for scoring large numbers of goals, but when he does, they are usually spectacular or important. Or both, as in the Europa League final last season for Aston Villa against Freiburg. Tielemans scored just ten times for his former club in 134 matches. In addition, he added only 28 strikes in 195 games for Leicester City, but one of them was the winning goal in the 2021 FA Cup final. Man United goal Tielemans thought he had opened his account last month against Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford, but the goal was ruled out. Nonetheless, he finally got on the scoresheet during his 14th match for the club, having been an ever-present so far this season. The Belgian midfielder pulled his side level at 2-2 just before half time against Aston Villa when Zion Suzuki could not keep out the effort. His muted celebrations were out of respect for his former team, even though he must have been delighted to open his account in front of the Stretford End in such dramatic circumstances. The club’s official website has also reported on why the goal was special. The site reports, “it’s taken pretty extensive research but, by our reckoning, no United man has ever scored his first Premier League goal for the club against a former side.” Teddy Sheringham also almost did in August 1997 against Tottenham Hotspur, but his penalty cannoned off the post and out. Ralph Milne did achieve this in 1988 when he scored his first United goal against his former side Charlton Athletic. Tommy Boyle also scored in 1929 against his former side Sheffield United, and George Livingston in 1909 against his old team, Manchester City.

item.title: All quiet on extension front as Sal Stewart's value rises with award
item.description: LAS VEGAS – Sal Stewart’s Rookie of the Year award brought good news and bad news for the Cincinnati Reds this week. The good news is that thanks to new rules in the game meant to disincentivize service-time manipulation the Reds get an additional draft pick between the first and second rounds. The not-so-good news: The price just went up on the inevitable extension talks with the hard-hitting, 22-year-old All-Star. Reds GM meetings 4 great free agent fits for Cincinnati Reds as MLB's GM meetings open Four months after the Reds inked Stewart’s pal, Reds ace Chase Burns, to a $105 million, seven-year extension, the Reds and Stewart still had not engaged in talks about an extension for the 32-homer rookie slugger, sources said. And the meter continues to run after Stewart became the franchise’s ninth player to win the National League Rookie of the Year award, with Stewart also a finalist for a prestigious Silver Slugger award. Those winners are announced next week. The tangible upside for the team — beyond possibly earning a few more ticket sales in marketing the “award-winning” Sal — is the Prospect Promotion Incentive draft pick that figures to be a top-40 overall pick between their first- and second-round picks. That’s because of a 2022 rule that rewards teams for promoting prospects closer to the beginning of a season rather than wait long enough with their better prospects to assure an additional year of club control before free agency. That delay of less than two weeks led to players such as Kris Bryant and Maikel Franco to file union grievances a decade ago against their teams for service-time manipulation that delayed their free agency. Bryant won a Rookie of the Year award in 2015 after being kept in the minors the first eight games of that season, which meant an additional six years before he was eligible for free agency. How potentially valuable are the additional supplemental picks? Stewart was selected 32nd overall in 2022 – as an additional compensation pick for the Reds for losing Nick Castellanos as a free agent. item.title: 'Leicester draw is game for the fans and for Dover'
item.description: Dover manager Jake Leberl said the club would embrace the occasion [BBC] The manager of non-league Dover Athletic says the club's FA Cup draw against former Premier League champions Leicester City is "a game for the fans and for the town". Manager Jake Leberl described it as an "unbelievable draw". "[I'm] so pleased for everyone - the chairman who's been here so many years pumping money in, the new investors, and the fans who've had it hard for quite a few years," he said. Chairman of the sixth division side, Jim Parmenter, told BBC Radio Kent : "This is just one off in every 10 years." Leberl said his first thought was: "I would love to get to the third round." He said that would be "incredibly hard", adding: "But what a day and obviously financially brilliant for the club." The second round match between Dover and the 2021 FA Cup champions will take place on the weekend starting 4 December. The match against the League One side has drawn comparisons to Dover's 2015 FA Cup tie at home against Crystal Palace, who won 4-0 . Leberl, who was assistant manager at the time, said: "Football-wise [it is an] incredibly difficult game, but it's a game for the fans and for the town and we'll just embrace it and do the best we can." Parmenter said it would be "a fantastic day" for all the supporters. "But particularly [it is] a reward for all the volunteers, the hard working staff we've got here that have stuck with the club all through the tough times, the downs, the Covid situation, the points deductions, the fines, everything else," he added. Leicester City won the FA Cup in 2021 [Getty Images] In the FA Cup, second round winners receive £79,500 in prize money, while £21,200 is given to the losing side. The chairman said he hoped the money would act as a "platform for us to move the club forward". "It's a cup game, it's 90 minutes of football, our squad's right on top of their game at the moment, we're scoring goals, we're defending well, so why shouldn't we have a go and try to win the tie?" he added. 'Everything is possible' Fan Lynne Lister, who was at the club to watch the draw, agreed with the chairman. "The atmosphere in here tonight tells you how pleased we are with our draw," she added. "Everything is possible." Fellow fan Jamie Skeggs said it was a "dream tie" for the club. "The players have put in so much hard work and they deserve this, the fans deserve this after all the financial troubles we've had over the years," he added. "They may be ex-Premier League champions but they're coming to Crabble on a non-league pitch, they're not going to like it, so we'll see what happens." The asking price is considered to be similar to Jonathan Taylor.” Butler wrote on Monday evening. The most surprising part of the report, which has yet to be verified by the team or one of the NFL’s top insiders, is that the Ravens are supposedly looking for similar draft compensation to that of Taylor. The 32-year old, who will be 33 before the playoffs start in mid-January, has regressed from the season prior, where he managed 1,595 rushing yards and 5.2 yards per carry. This season, he has 689 rushing yards and has managed just 3.9 yards per carry. He ranked 2nd in the league in rushing yards in 2025, and ranks 7th in 2026. But a second round pick and more for a player about to turn 33 is borderline absurd, even for a contender like Green Bay who desperately need help at RB. Whilst the All-Pro back has managed to defy nature and running back carries rules that apply for virtually every other player at the position, his 2026 numbers have started to show father time gaining some ground on even the most stubborn bodies. At this point, anything much more than a deferred third rounder (2028 or 2029) and change would be a vast overpay for a player now seemingly officially out of his prime. item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images The Golden State Warriors are on a winning streak of eight after dropping their first three games, and they have a surprise All-Star contender to thank for it. The latest win against the New Orleans Pelicans was the biggest one yet, with the Golden State Warriors winning 138-87. It allowed for some much-needed rest for their star players, which is priceless at this stage of the season, and also allowed lesser-heralded players to showcase their talent. Chris Mullin said after the game that one such player is firmly on All-Star watch after the win against the Pelicans, and nobody saw it coming. Chris Mullin hails Yaxel Lendeborg With every game, Mike Dunleavy Jr. is being made to look like a genius by Yaxel Lendeborg, and that continued against the Pelicans. Lendeborg bounced back from some poor shooting nights with a scorching 23 points on just 14 shots, making all four of his threes. In addition, he had seven rebounds and four assists as he continued to do the basics of the game well, especially for a rookie. The 11th pick in the draft should be the runaway contender for Rookie of the Year, and in Chris Mullin’s opinion, that’s such a given that All-Star conversations should begin now. He said (via Warriors on NBCS ): “There’s no one forcing anything. The ball is doing the work. Yaxel, we keep talking about rookie watch? We are on All-Star watch. They are All-Star numbers for one of the best teams in the league!” Through the first ten games of his NBA career, Lendeborg is averaging 21.2 points, 7.2 rebounds, and four assists while shooting more than 40% on 3PT, on a team that is setting the pace surprisingly in the West. item.description: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry reacts after scoring during the first half of his team's win over the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday at Chase Center. (Heather Diehl/Associated Press) When all else failed, there was another end of the court to hang the hat on, as the thinking went. Toughness. Teeth. New point-of-attack vigor, brought by new defensive mind Frank Vogel. And yet three games and three losses brought an embarrassing swath of defensive breakdowns in the pick-and-roll, and too many bodies lost on weak-side rotations (cough, Yaxel Lendeborg ), and these Golden State Warriors looked lost. Steve Kerr 's shift to more five-out offensive "Flow," as Golden State calls it , was bound to lead to offensive clunkiness. Through three games, though, points were hardly the issue. Golden State had 127 dumped on them by the Lakers in the season opener, and then were torched by the Grizzlies' Ty Jerome, and then watched Devin Booker run rampant in Phoenix. "You got to create an identity," Draymond Green said Oct. 26. "And we haven't created that identity yet." Exactly two weeks later, late in the second quarter of the Warriors'138-87 beatdown, a depleted and hapless New Orleans Pelicans team attempted to play advantage basketball. New Orleans center Derik Queen had his back in the post to the decidedly smaller De'Anthony Melton, with no promise of a double-team coming. Queen made his move, naturally, and spun off Melton toward what appeared as a wide-open lane. And Warriors center Charles Bassey, sliding over under the rim, leaped with Queen and sent a two-hand dunk attempt back. Has this Golden State team, which completed a 6-0 homstand, found its identity? Still not yet, if you asked Kerr earlier Monday night. They're 11 games in, after all. But identities are both forged in the fires of close games and in sleepy halls against teams with no identity; these Warriors have cultivated a growing reputation for nastiness across a now-eight-game winning streak full of skirmishes and technicals, and utterly shut down the Pelicans' entire operation in ferocious style Monday. item.title: ‘You don’t get to’: Udonis Haslem shares what he privately said to Giannis Antetokounmpo
item.description: Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images The Miami Heat haven’t had a great start to the season despite bringing in Giannis Antetokounmpo in a blockbuster trade in the summer. The 31-year-old, individually, has done what he needs to do in most games, but the Heat are still 4-6 this season, which is not great at all. That could easily make Antetokounmpo wonder if he made the right decision and sulk, but Heat legend Udonis Haslem personally offered him some advice. Udonis Haslem’s advice to Giannis Antetokounmpo about Miami Heat’s adversity When Antetokounmpo joined the Miami Heat in the summer, he would’ve hoped for a much better start than what he has seen. The Heat lost each of their first four games of the season, and even though they have won four of their next six, there are still several concerns about how good they are. Haslem, who experienced all of that during his 20-year career with the Miami Heat, spoke to Antetokounmpo this week about dealing with adversity. The 46-year-old, who works as the vice president of basketball development with the Heat, explained his advice to the Greek Freak on Dwyane Wade’s podcast. He said: “I told Giannis today: ‘Listen, you don’t get to pick and choose when the adversity hits. You just pick and choose how you respond.’ “Some people have it at the beginning of the season, some people are going to have it in the middle of the season, and some people are going to have it at the end. You don’t pick and choose when the adversity hits. You just pick and choose how you respond. “Ok, we’re having it early. Let’s get it out of the way then. That’s fine. Let’s get it out now. “Some people are going to get in the middle, and some people are going to get hit in the end. You don’t want to be the ones who get hit by adversity in the end. You don’t want that. If anything, if you can choose, you want to choose that now.” Haslem definitely has a point, but the Heat’s defensive problems don’t quite seem like temporary adversity. They feel like they need a lot of work, and there’s no easy fix. That will take time, but Antetokounmpo’s dominance, just like he showed against the Sacramento Kings, will be key to getting wins on the board while they try to fix their defence. In four of the last six games, that has worked, but it remains to be seen if they can sustain it for a longer period.
